title: 1952 Luxembourg Agreement — German material reparations after the Holocaust

decision_cutoff.date_or_period: 1952-09-08, immediately before the Federal Cabinet vote on agenda items 1–2 of its 245th meeting
decision_cutoff.definition: Pre-approval review of the negotiated German-Israeli agreement and Claims Conference protocols, after the recorded briefings and debate but before the Cabinet resolution; signature, ratification and delivery remain outside the cutoff. The meeting ran 09:30–12:35 local time; the vote minute is not established.
decision_cutoff.evidence_receipt: The minutes identify the documents before the Cabinet and the oral briefings. This establishes receipt of those materials by the Cabinet, not receipt of every contextual claim in the packet.

sources.citation: Konrad Adenauer, Bundestag statement on German responsibility and restitution, 27 September 1951
sources.use_note: Contemporaneous West German acknowledgement of crimes committed in Germany's name and commitment to material restitution, while rejecting collective personal guilt of all Germans.

sources.citation: Conference on Jewish Material Claims Against Germany, History of the Claims Conference / Luxembourg Agreements
sources.use_note: Documents negotiations, survivor representation and the compensation/restitution framework.

sources.citation: Claims Conference, 70th Anniversary of the Luxembourg Agreements
sources.use_note: Summarises the agreements' structure, opposition and long-run compensation significance.

sources.citation: German Federal Government / historical materials on the Luxembourg Agreement and Wiedergutmachung
sources.use_note: Successor-state perspective on reparations and agreement implementation.

sources.citation: Federal Cabinet, 245th meeting, 8 September 1952, agenda items 1–2
sources.use_note: PDF pp. 2–7: received negotiating materials and pre-vote funding disagreement; final vote and retrospective editorial notes excluded from decision premises.
Direct primary replacement for legacy Adenauer URL; acknowledgement and partial restitution, not a general finding of citizen innocence.

sources.citation: Knesset debate, 7 January 1952, document 18 in Yaakov Sharett (ed.), The Reparations Controversy (2011), pp. 161–164,178–187
sources.use_note: Primary speeches reconstructed through an explicitly abridged translation: resettlement claim and opposition positions, not measured survivor prevalence or independently audited costs.

correction_11_admission.reason: Pre-vote event is pinned, but detailed needs, destroyed-record mechanisms and contextual receipt remain incompletely supported; no complete historical admission certificate.
